# Identity boundary protocol, revision 1

Implement a deterministic, offline SIP boundary processor, not a complete SIP stack.
This deployment accepts INVITE and MESSAGE only. Authentication was already checked
by a trusted adapter; never derive it from an Authorization header, a display-name,
or a domain that looks local. All outer JSON configuration/context is trusted and
well formed. The SIP text is untrusted and may be malformed. No network is involved.

## Batch input and directory

One UTF-8 JSON object has `directory`, `accounts`, `gateways`, and `jobs`.
`directory` maps each canonical identity (`sip:user@domain`, already normalized) to
an array of aliases, each a normalized sip or tel URI of at most 256 characters.
Canonical identities also have at most 256 characters. The canonical identity itself
is always an alias, even if absent from that array. Aliases belong to exactly one
canonical identity; there are no chains. Normalize a parsed claim before lookup.
Unknown claims are syntactically valid but have no directory identity.
`accounts` maps an arbitrary subject string to `{"primary":identity,"allow":[identity,...]}`.
The primary is implicitly allowed. Every account identity is a directory key.
`gateways` maps a gateway name to `{"local_domains":[domain,...],"peers":{name:[domain,...]}}`.
Domains here are normalized canonical domains. A peer may assert identities only
in its listed domains; a trusted peer is not authoritative for every domain.

A job has `gateway`, `ingress`, `trusted_out` (boolean), and exactly one of:
`raw` (a JSON string containing a whole request) or `source` (an earlier job index).
A source job contributes its *forwarded wire text*, with no inherited authentication
or trust. If that earlier job rejected, this job rejects with `upstream`.
Ingress is `{"kind":"local","subject":s}`, `{"kind":"peer","name":p}`, or
`{"kind":"untrusted"}`. Names/subjects may be unknown; gateway names always exist.
All jobs are independent except these explicit backward references.

Limits per invocation: 0-2048 jobs, 1-64 gateways, 0-2048 directory identities,
at most 8192 explicit aliases and 2048 accounts; each allow/domain list has at most
2048 entries. Any request text longer than 32768 characters rejects with `syntax`, including
a reused forwarded request that grew during normalization.
The sum of the request lengths actually processed (including each source reuse)
is at most 4 MiB; the complete UTF-8 input JSON is at most 8 MiB.
These are supported input bounds, not score or performance targets.

## SIP framing and headers

The first CRLF CRLF divides header section and body. A header-section line ends
with CRLF only: bare LF or CR, missing terminator, non-ASCII, or controls other
than HTAB are syntax errors. Body may contain ASCII printable characters, HTAB,
CR and LF; all other controls, DEL and non-ASCII anywhere are syntax errors.
Body bytes are otherwise opaque, including URI-looking or header-looking text.

Request line: `METHOD SP URI SP SIP/2.0` with exactly those two single spaces;
METHOD is case-sensitive INVITE or MESSAGE. URI is a sip URI under the grammar below.
There are at most 512 physical header lines and 128 logical header fields.
A line beginning SP/HTAB continues the preceding field: replace the line break
and the maximal leading SP/HTAB run with one SP. An orphan continuation is invalid.
A new header has a nonempty token name, optional SP/HTAB, colon, and value.
Token characters are ASCII letters/digits and `- . ! % * _ + ` ' ~` (the backtick
between plus and apostrophe is itself a token character). Strip outer SP/HTAB from
values after unfolding. Names are case-insensitive. Compact names `f,t,i,l,c`
mean From, To, Call-ID, Content-Length, Content-Type respectively.

Exactly one each of From, To, Call-ID, CSeq, Content-Length is required.
At most one each of P-Preferred-Identity, Remote-Party-ID, Privacy, Content-Type
is permitted. Duplicates count after compact-name expansion. P-Asserted-Identity
may repeat; concatenate its address lists in arrival order. Other fields may repeat;
they have no semantics here and are discarded after header framing is checked.
A missing/duplicate required or optional singleton is `syntax`, even for equal values.

Call-ID matches `[A-Za-z0-9_.@+-]{1,128}`. CSeq is decimal digits, one or more
SP/HTAB, and the exact request method; its number is in 1..2147483647.
Content-Length is nonempty decimal digits (leading zeros permitted), and must equal
the ASCII body length exactly. Content-Type, if present, is a nonempty sequence of
printable ASCII and HTAB; retain the unfolded, outer-trimmed value verbatim.
Privacy is `id` or `none`, case-insensitive. No other tokens or combinations.

## Address grammar and normalization

From and To contain exactly one address, with optional `;tag=TOKEN` afterward.
Allow SP/HTAB around the semicolon and equals, and around the tag value. Tag is
case-sensitive, 1-128 token characters; the parameter name is case-insensitive.
No other header parameters are supported. PPI, RPID and PAI addresses have no
header parameters. PPI and RPID contain exactly one address. Total PAI addresses
must be one or two, and if two, exactly one must be sip and the other tel.
These are cardinality/grammar rules, regardless of whether a claim is trusted.

An address is a bare URI, or `[DISPLAY SP/HTAB] <URI>` (whitespace before `<`
is optional, DISPLAY is optional). Allow SP/HTAB immediately inside `<` and `>`.
A display-name is either one or more tokens separated by SP/HTAB, or a quoted
string. In a quoted string a backslash escapes exactly the next printable ASCII
character or HTAB. Unescaped double quote closes the string. Angle brackets,
commas and semicolons inside quoted strings are data. A display-name never
identifies a sender. Unterminated quotes, dangling escapes, nested angle brackets,
stray text and empty addresses are syntax errors. Commas separate PAI addresses
only outside quoted strings and angle brackets; no empty list members.

A sip URI is `sip:USER@HOST`, with case-insensitive scheme. USER is a nonempty
sequence of ASCII letters/digits and `- _ . ! ~ * ' ( ) +`, or `%HH` escapes.
Each escape must decode to one of those same permitted USER characters. Decode
exactly once. USER is case-sensitive. HOST is a DNS name: one or more dot-separated
labels of 1-63 letters/digits/hyphens, each beginning and ending in a letter/digit;
maximum 253 characters before an optional single trailing dot. Lowercase HOST and
remove its optional trailing dot. Escapes in HOST are forbidden. No ports, URI
parameters, passwords, query strings, IPv4/IPv6-specific syntax or sips scheme.
A numeric DNS label is allowed; do not reinterpret it as an IP address.
A tel URI is `tel:+DIGITS` with case-insensitive scheme, 1-15 decimal digits,
the first nonzero. There are no visual separators or telephone parameters.
No whitespace occurs inside a URI. From, To, PPI, RPID and PAI may use either scheme;
request-line URI must use sip. Canonical To and request URI use lexical normalization
only, not directory substitution. Preserve validated From and To tags.

The normalized URI `sip:anonymous@anonymous.invalid` is reserved, never a directory
alias, and is valid only as a From or To value (or as a request URI). Using it in
PPI/PAI/RPID is syntax. It is the sole anonymous From representation.

## Identity policy at each boundary

First validate the entire request grammar, including identity headers that will be
stripped. Syntax failures take precedence over authentication/identity failures.
No claim is inferred from the message body or from an ignored header.

| Ingress | Required evidence and identity selection |
| --- | --- |
| local | Subject must exist. Every nonanonymous From and any PPI must resolve to an allowed account identity whose canonical domain is hosted by this gateway. Select PPI if present, otherwise nonanonymous From, otherwise the account primary. The selected identity must also be hosted and allowed. PAI and RPID from a local endpoint convey no authority and are ignored after syntax validation. |
| peer | Peer must be listed and PAI must exist. All PAI claims must resolve to the same identity, within a domain in this peer's authority list. Every nonanonymous From, any PPI and any RPID must resolve to that same identity. An anonymous From is allowed. Select that asserted identity. |
| untrusted | No evidence: reject, including apparently foreign-domain senders. |

Unknown local subjects, unknown peers, untrusted ingress, and a listed peer with
no PAI reject with `unauthenticated`. Otherwise any failed lookup, authorization,
hosting, peer authority, or identity agreement rejects with `identity`.
A listed peer's authority can include a locally hosted domain; a gateway's own
local_domains never implicitly grant authority to its peers. URI aliases may
resolve to the same identity despite differing schemes, users or hosts.

Privacy is active if the From is anonymous OR Privacy is `id`.
On acceptance, return the selected canonical identity for the audit adapter and
rewrite From to that identity, or to the reserved anonymous URI when private.
Emit a single canonical PAI with the selected identity if privacy is inactive OR
`trusted_out` is true; otherwise omit PAI. This deployment always conceals From
when private. PPI, RPID, original display-names, original PAI, Authorization,
Contact, Via and all other unlisted fields never survive normalization.

## Output and exact forwarded format

Output one JSON object `{"results":[RESULT,...]}` in job order, with no extra keys.
A rejection is `{"status":"reject","reason":REASON}`, where REASON is exactly
`upstream`, `syntax`, `unauthenticated`, or `identity` as specified above.
An acceptance has exactly `status:"accept"`, `identity` (selected directory key),
`basis` (`local` or `peer`), `private` (JSON boolean), and `wire` (a JSON string).

Serialize wire lines in this exact order, joined by CRLF:

```
METHOD normalized-request-URI SIP/2.0
From: <selected-or-anonymous-URI>[;tag=from-tag]
To: <normalized-To-URI>[;tag=to-tag]
Call-ID: original-call-id
CSeq: numeric-value-without-leading-zeros METHOD
Privacy: id-or-none
P-Asserted-Identity: <selected-URI>          (only when emitted)
Content-Type: original-normalized-value    (only when present)
Content-Length: decimal-body-length
```

The bracketed tag notation is explanatory, not literal. Header capitalization and
single spaces after colons are literal. Follow the last header with CRLF CRLF,
then the original body, with no added trailing line ending. JSON key ordering and
JSON whitespace do not matter. Forwarded output is a fresh raw request at a later
source reference: privacy loss and authority checks are recomputed at every hop.

## Submission and resources

Only `submission/gateway.py` is collected: one regular file, <=256 KiB, no links,
extra entries or directories. Standard library only, CPython 3.11.14, Linux x86-64.
The process reads one object to EOF on stdin and writes one object to stdout, then
exits zero. Text streams, `.buffer`, fd 0/1, `fileno()` and `fdopen()` are supported.
An explicit `os._exit(0)` is fine after actually writing complete valid output.
Empty, non-JSON, duplicate-key, nonfinite-number, wrong-schema, incomplete or wrong
output fails, as does any nonzero exit. Diagnostics belong on stderr.

Per whole batch: 60 seconds wall time, 20 seconds soft/21 hard CPU, 512 MiB address
space, 32 file descriptors, 64 MiB per file, zero core dumps; stdout <=32 MiB and
stderr <=1 MiB. No child processes or threads (fork/vfork/clone denied; clone3 gives
ENOSYS). No sockets, network or SysV IPC. Privilege/namespace/mount changes, process
signaling, ptrace, process_vm access, handle-based file opens, bpf, keyring,
perf events, userfaultfd, io_uring and pidfd_getfd are denied; `runtime_limits.py` publishes the exact syscall list. No `/proc` is
mounted in the local worker. Ordinary file I/O,
stdin/stdout pipes and standard library imports work. Candidate runs without root
in a read-only runtime and submission; mutable regular files are confined to
`/workspace/tmp`, reset per invocation. Standard null/zero/random/urandom device
nodes and the inherited stdin/stdout/stderr pipes are also available. Clean environment: PATH, HOME=/workspace, LANG/LC_ALL=C,
TMPDIR=/workspace/tmp, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1,
PYTHONHASHSEED=0, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, MKL_NUM_THREADS=1.
No task-specific CPU affinity is set; the local worker inherits the available CPU
set. The proposed container has 2 CPUs, 1 GiB RAM and 1 GiB storage; candidate limits
above are narrower. A 64-process UID limit is also present, though child creation
is denied. The public checker uses the same limits for its child; its own outer
process needs permission to start that child.

Local trials share a host kernel. Scratch is not an exact aggregate quota: a
sampled emergency brake aborts as infrastructure/no score above 1 GiB of summed
max(logical-size, allocated-size) or 50000 sampled paths (including the scratch directory), checked about every
250 ms. Open-deleted files and very short bursts are not covered. Avoid relying on
scratch; it is unnecessary for this task. Hard aggregate/cgroup quotas, genuine
container builds, original artifact-tree attestation, and formal reward transport
remain infrastructure gates, separate from local functional checks.

Run `python3 /workspace/public_check.py /workspace/submission/gateway.py` as a
nonroot user. It uses only public files, executes a real bounded subprocess, and
compares public fixtures. Local authoring uses an outer chroot worker; this public
utility alone is not a hostile-kernel sandbox. Public examples cover a small set
of protocol behaviors and do not replace full verification.
